Scope and inclusion criteria:

- Version constraint: Use the last page revision from June 2023 (e.g., most recent timestamp within June 2023 for each page).
- A "Twitter/X post citation" means a reference directly to a tweet URL (twitter.com/[user]/status/[id] or x.com/[user]/status/[id]) or an archived URL that resolves to such a tweet.
- Exclusions: User profiles, lists, search pages, or any Twitter links not pointing to a specific tweet.

- Include: web.archive.org/.../https://twitter.com/user/status/456 with archive timestamp or template date indicating August.

I propose we use MediaWiki API to retrieve the last June 2023 revision per page. Pseudocode:

1) For each title in ["August 1" ... "August 31"], request revisions with rvstart=2023-06-30T23:59:59Z and rvdir=older, rvlimit=1, rvprop=ids|timestamp|content.
2) Store the revision id and timestamp.

Example Python snippet:

import requests

API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"

def last_june_rev(title):
    params = {
        "action": "query",
        "format": "json",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "titles": title,
        "rvstart": "2023-06-30T23:59:59Z",
        "rvdir": "older",
        "rvlimit": 1,
        "rvprop": "ids|timestamp"
    }
    r = requests.get(API, params=params).json()
    pages = r.get("query", {}).get("pages", {})
    for _, p in pages.items():
        revs = p.get("revisions", [])
        if revs:
            return {
                "title": title,
                "revid": revs[0]["revid"],
                "timestamp": revs[0]["timestamp"]
            }
    return None

Next, we fetch the wikitext for these revisions and do a first-pass detection of Twitter/X citations using a simple regex for twitter.com URLs. I'll include x.com and archived forms in a later refinement.

Python idea:

import requests, re
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
TW_REGEX = re.compile(r"https?://(?:www\.)?twitter\.com/[^/]+/status/\d+")

revids = [115123001, 115129876, 115104443]

results = {}
for rid in revids:
    r = requests.get(API, params={
        "action": "query",
        "format": "json",
        "prop": "revisions",
        "revids": rid,
        "rvprop": "content"
    }).json()
    pages = r.get("query", {}).get("pages", {})
    for _, p in pages.items():
        revs = p.get("revisions", [])
        if revs:
            content = revs[0].get("*", "") or revs[0].get("slots", {}).get("main", {}).get("*", "")
            matches = TW_REGEX.findall(content)
            results[rid] = len(set(matches))

print(results)

Please run and report counts per revision; we will map revisions back to page titles afterwards.
